title: pvSPHDatasetInterpolator
body:
## pvSPHDatasetInterpolator

Interpolates particle data with smoothed-particle-hydrodynamics kernels: the Input is the particle set (a point set with point arrays, normally including density and optionally mass) and the Source is any dataset whose points receive the SPH-weighted values. The output keeps Source's structure and adds the interpolated arrays, a Shepard-sum array (on by default) and any derivative arrays. Use it to post-process SPH simulation output on meshes, slices or images; for non-SPH scattered data use pvPointDatasetInterpolator.

Common mistakes and assumptions:

- The kernel SpatialStep (smoothing length h) defaults to 0.0001; set it to the simulation's smoothing length in dataset units, or neighbourhoods are tiny and most output points become null points.
- DensityArray defaults to the name Rho; name your particle density array if it differs.
- Schemaxis generates this binding from ParaView's catalogue; it has not run a native acceptance check for this operation.

Native constructor: `SPHDatasetInterpolator`. Identity: `filters/SPHDatasetInterpolator`. Role: `pipeline`. Output kinds: `["data"]`.

### Inputs

| Port | Meaning / native port | Required | Multiplicity | Kind | Contract |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Input` | Required data input for the native Input port. Give the name of the upstream node to connect, or a {node, port} object to use another of its output ports. ParaView: The data source to be interpolated onto the *Source*. Accepted data: explicit-point datasets (polygonal, unstructured or structured grids) (vtkPointSet). The input needs at least one point-centred array with 1 component. The input needs at least one point-centred array. | True | one object | `data` | `{"compatibility":"native-domain-checked","composite":null,"cost":{"basis":"no benchmark","conversion":"none inserted","rating":"unknown"},"nativeTypes":["vtkPointSet"],"requirements":{},"traits":{"contiguity":"unknown","indexing":"unknown","iteration":"unknown"}}` |
| `Source` | Required data input for the native Source port. Give the name of the upstream node to connect, or a {node, port} object to use another of its output ports. ParaView: The data source that provides the structure to be interpolated on. Accepted data: any dataset (meshes, grids, point sets) (vtkDataSet). | True | one object | `data` | `{"compatibility":"native-domain-checked","composite":null,"cost":{"basis":"no benchmark","conversion":"none inserted","rating":"unknown"},"nativeTypes":["vtkDataSet"],"requirements":{},"traits":{"contiguity":"unknown","indexing":"unknown","iteration":"unknown"}}` |

### Options

| Key | Meaning / native assignment | Type and constraints | Default / required | Example value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ComputeShepardSum` | Indicate whether to compute the summation of Shepard coefficients. In the interior of a SPH point cloud, the Shephard summation value should be ~1.0. Towards the boundary, the Shepard summation is less than 1.0. If ComputeShepardSum is specified, then the output will contain an array of summed Shepard weights for each output point. | `{"type":"boolean"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `false` |
| `CutoffArray` | Specify the Cutoff array name. If not specified, then the radius at each point will be computed as cutoff factor * smoothing length at a each point. | `{"type":"string"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `"REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"` |
| `DensityArray` | Specify the density array name. This is required in computation. If not specified the code will error out. | `{"type":"string"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `"REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"` |
| `DerivativeArrays` | Specify the arrays whose derivative is to be taken. If the name of the array is "derivArray" this will produce an output array with the name "derivArray_deriv" (after filter execution). | `{"items":{"type":"string"},"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `["REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"]` |
| `ExcludedArrays` | Specify arrays which are to be excluded from the interpolation process. | `{"items":{"type":"string"},"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `["REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"]` |
| `Kernel` | Smoothing kernel W(r, h) used to weight neighbouring particles, following D.J. Price's SPH formulations. All four take the kernel options SpatialStep (the smoothing length h, in dataset units) and Dimension (1 to 3, the dimension of the particle problem, which sets the normalization). They differ in order and support radius: SPH Cubic Kernel (cutoff 2h, cheapest and least smooth), SPH Quartic Kernel (2.5h), SPH Quintic Kernel (3h, higher order, the ParaView default) and SPH Wendland Quintic Kernel (2h, a compactly supported Wendland function). Pick the kernel your SPH solver used so interpolated values are consistent with the simulation. | `{"type":"typed proxy","choices":["SPH Cubic Kernel","SPH Quartic Kernel","SPH Quintic Kernel","SPH Wendland Quintic Kernel"]}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `{"type":"SPH Cubic Kernel"}` |
| `Locator` | Specify a point locator. | `{"type":"typed proxy","choices":["Static Point Locator"]}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `{"type":"Static Point Locator"}` |
| `MassArray` | Specify the mass array name. If not specified, then the mass at each point will be computed from the density and local (spherical) volume at a each point. | `{"type":"string"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `"REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"` |
| `NullPointsStrategy` | Specify a strategy to use when encountering a "null" point during the interpolation process. Null points occur when the local neighborhood (of nearby points to interpolate from) is empty. If the strategy is set to MaskPoints, then an output array is created that marks points as being valid (=1) or null (invalid =0) (and the NullValue is set as well). If the strategy is set to NullValue, then the output data value(s) are set to the NullPoint value (specified in the output point data). | `{"type":"enum","values":["Mask Points","Null Value"]}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `"Mask Points"` |
| `NullValue` | Specify the null point value. When a null point is encountered then all components of each null tuple are set to this value. By default the null value is set to zero. | `{"type":"number"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `1` |
| `PassCellArrays` | Indicate whether to shallow copy the input cell data arrays to the output. | `{"type":"boolean"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `false` |
| `PassFieldArrays` | Indicate whether to shallow copy the input field data arrays to the output. | `{"type":"boolean"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `false` |
| `PassPointArrays` | Indicate whether to shallow copy the input point data arrays to the output. | `{"type":"boolean"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `false` |
| `ShepardSumArrayName` | If ComputeShepardSum is on, then an array is generated with name ShepardSumArrayName for each input point. This vtkFloatArray is placed into the output of the filter, and NullPoints have value =0.0. The default name is "Shepard Summation". | `{"type":"string"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `"REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"` |
| `ValidPointsMaskArrayName` | If the NullPointsStrategy is "Mask Points", then an array is generated for each input point. This vtkCharArray is placed into the output of the filter, with a non-zero value for a valid point, and zero otherwise. The name of this masking array is specified here. | `{"type":"string"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `"REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"` |

### Nested `Kernel` → `SPH Cubic Kernel`

Syntax: `{"type":"SPH Cubic Kernel","options":{...}}`. Native identity: `point_interpolation_kernels/SPHCubicKernel`. Omitted nested options retain native values on subsequent visits.

| Key | Meaning / native assignment | Type and constraints | Default / required | Example value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Kernel.options.Dimension` | Spatial dimension of the particle data (1, 2 or 3). It selects the kernel’s normalization constant and the power of SpatialStep used for the default particle volume (SpatialStep^Dimension). Use 2 for planar simulations and 3 for volumetric ones. | `{"maximum":3,"minimum":1,"type":"integer"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `1` |
| `Kernel.options.SpatialStep` | Smoothing length h of the kernel in dataset units. Neighbours are gathered within 2 × h of each sample (unless the operation supplies a cutoff array), weights are normalized by h^Dimension, and without a mass array each particle’s volume is taken as h^Dimension. Set it to the smoothing length or initial particle spacing of your simulation. | `{"minimum":0.0,"type":"number"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `0.0` |

### Nested `Locator` → `Static Point Locator`

Syntax: `{"type":"Static Point Locator","options":{...}}`. Native identity: `point_locators/StaticPointLocator`. Omitted nested options retain native values on subsequent visits.

| Key | Meaning / native assignment | Type and constraints | Default / required | Example value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Locator.options.Automatic` | When true, the locator derives its bucket grid from the number of source points and NumberOfPointsPerBucket; when false, it uses Divisions exactly. | `{"type":"boolean"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `false` |
| `Locator.options.Divisions` | Bucket counts [nx, ny, nz] along x, y and z, used only when Automatic is false. Very fine grids waste memory on sparse clouds; very coarse grids make each search scan many points. | `{"items":{"type":"integer"},"maxItems":3,"minItems":3,"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `[1,1,1]` |
| `Locator.options.NumberOfPointsPerBucket` | Average number of source points per bucket targeted when Automatic is true; smaller values create more, smaller buckets. Ignored when Automatic is false. | `{"minimum":1,"type":"integer"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `1` |
